item.title: The Voodoo Wiimote
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A Nintendo Wii remote which acts as a voodoo doll on whomever or whatever its user is thinking about, so long as:

  • The Wii console the remote is paired to is powered on.
  • The remote is not connected to a Nunchuk peripheral.
  • The remote’s batteries are at least half full.

Central Narrative: A Nintendo Wii console was hooked up to a break room TV at Site-23. Almost immediately after, a researcher suffered severe injuries when one of the console’s remotes was sent flying into the TV. A security officer ordered for the console to be removed and disposed of, but submitted the previously mentioned remote to the labs for research. Soon after this, the object was registered as an SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Wii remote is mysterious in that there is very little potential for explaining its anomalous properties, and that it has potential use to the Foundation as a means of keeping peace at its sites.

Additional Notes: I wasn’t able to find any SCPs similar to this concept, so I was hoping critics could let me know if there are.

item.title: The Hungry Computer
item.content:encoded:
Item#: SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Safe

Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is stored at Site-23 in a standard anomalous object containment room that is 6m x 6m x 10m. The room is to be visually surveyed 24 hours a day. The anomalous object containment room is to be locked with a biometric lock that is coded to Level 3 and above. Any contact with SCP-XXXX is to be done with full body coverings. Gloves are 100% necessary if full body coverings are unavailable in an emergency.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a standard computer array that consists of one (1) unbranded monitor, one day (1) unbranded mouse, one (1) unbranded keyboard, and one (1) unbranded computer tower. SCP-XXXX appears to be a completely normal computer set-up that runs at standard levels for such a device at initial observation. Personnel interacting with SCP-XXXX cannot derive any difference between SCP-XXXX and a non-anomalous computer array. SCP-XXXX anomalous property can be observed when opening the computer case. The inner workings of SCP-XXXX are completely biological. The exterior “shell” is made up of chitin and bone. SCP-XXXX's tower has a heart that pumps blood throughout the biological “circuitry” of SCP-XXXX. Inside of the case additionally contains portions of brain tissue. These sections of brain tissue seem to be the major component to SCP-XXXX's memory and processing. There are additionally some small, unidentified organs inside SCP-XXXX that require further study to ascertain their purpose, such as bladders of unknown fluid, and small portions that appear to be keratin without a clear function. SCP-XXXX does not require any external power. As to how SCP-XXXX is functional without a source of power is unknown. Anyone wearing gloves can open the case and handle SCP-XXXX without triggering SCP-XXXX's consumption state (See SCP-XXXX-1.a) SCP-XXXX has been known to bleed if some of the softer interior is lacerated or punctured. These lacerations or punctures will heal at a rate that is normal for biological entities. SCP-XXXX appears to be vulnerable to any and all circumstances that would harm any other biological entity unless damage caused is to the exterior. Any scratches and divots appearing in SCP-XXXX's “carapace” or case seem to be permanent with the only exception is a complete puncture. The interior will heal leaving a mark where it was punctured.

SCP-XXXX-1.a. Dr. Tam’s research into SCP-XXXX’s consumption process and status.

One (1) D-Class (D-15893) was told to sit in front of SCP-XXXX and research a topic of his choosing. After a defined amount of time, SCP-XXXX began consumption.

1.) SCP-XXXX's keyboard and mouse produce microscopic "hooks" that attach to the user.

2.) SCP-XXXX's keyboard and mouse then produce a flesh-like covering that starts to envelope the user. These also have microscopic hooks that keep the user (here on referred to as victim) from escaping.

3.) SCP-XXXX will then produce a toxin that has an anesthetic effect. This toxin will also start to dissolve any biological material it comes into contact with.

4.) The additional components of SCP-XXXX begin consuming and joining together, SCP-XXXX has no semblance of its initial state and appears as a fleshy mass.

5.) After the victim is completely enveloped, SCP-XXXX will dissolve the victim completely returning to its previous state until another victim attempts to use SCP-XXXX.

6.) After approximately 5 hours SCP-XXXX will then eject a disk from its previously empty disk drive. The contents of the disk are described below.

7.) SCP-XXXX seems to produce no solid waste after consumption but a heavy smell of *"burnt hair"* can be derived while SCP-XXXX is in the final stages of consumption. Since SCP-XXXX doesn't grow in size and only produces the aforementioned CD, it is unclear what happens to most of the mass consumed by SCP-XXXX's.

+ Contents of Ejected Disk
– hide block

Side Research Notes: SCP-XXXX-A1: Contents of Disk The contents of the disk ejected by SCP-XXXX after consumption can be played on any standard CD drive device. It is unknown how SCP-XXXX produces the materials needed to produce a completely normal Compact Disk. When the CD is placed in any CD drive one must navigate to the file location. Once the file is opened, there is a standard word document. Inside this document is the complete genetic make-up of the victim consumed. Researchers theorize that this could potentially be used to clone the consumed victim. After a thorough study of the CD by renowned SCP biological engineer, Dr. Darren [REDACTED], it appears that some of the genetic make up shows signs of degradation. This indicates that this particular genetic code is representative of the consumed victim at the exact age they were when consumed. The reason SCP-XXXX's CD's are not given an SCP designation is due to the fact that this file can be removed or erased from the CD and then can be used as any other blank CD.

+ Approx. time table of Consumption process
– hide block

Approximate Time Summery of SCP-XXXX’s Consumption:

0:00 - D-15893 told to sit.

0:47 - D-15893 begins research into “orca whales”. First contact with SCP-XXXX reported.

4:37 - D-15893 noticed hands were stuck to SCP-XXXX

6:12 - SCP-XXXX is seen starting to expand.

15:42 - D-15893 is approx. 50% enveloped by SCP-XXXX

28:19 - SCP-XXXX has completely enveloped D-15893

32:47 - Struggling inside SCP-XXXX has ceased.

45:55 - SCP-XXXX began retracting.

48:02 - Smell described as “burnt hair” begins to permeate the testing lab.

59:35 - SCP-XXXX once again appears in its default form.

+ Addendum: Recovery Notes
- hide this content

Addendum: Recovery Notes** SCP-XXXX was found in the basement of ████████, a known rapist and murderer, located in ████████, WA on the date ██/██/████. Found with SCP-XXXX were also several corpses of ████████ victims. It is unknown if SCP-XXXX was a normal computer that was transformed via an unknown cause or was built with the biological material from the corpses around it via an unknown builder. During ████████ arrest, he stated *"What the ████ is that thing! How did it get into my basement?!"* indicating that ████████ was not responsible for SCP-XXXX's presence. SCP recovery teams were called by Agent ████████ who was inserted into the ████████ ████████ Agency at the time undercover. After ████████ was detained by local law enforcement, Agent ████████ was part of the team conducting the crime scene investigation and found SCP-XXXX. SCP-XXXX was found feeding on the corpses in the basement when SCP Agent ████████ found it. This was vital in the recovery process as it led to no loss of life recovering SCP-XXXX. All parties present except SCP personnel were given Class D amnestics.

O5 command statement;
*"We have learned all we need to learn about how SCP-XXXX eats living things. I see no reason to waste more D-Class persons to feed it. I think the next step should be to let it sit in its containment and see if the power begins to fail. If that's the case, we'll "feed" it and see if that's what gives it power. Being clear, I DO NOT want you to let it die. Have a D-Class ready in case of an emergency feeding."*

Researcher Aaron ████████ appealed to change status of SCP-XXXX from Euclid to Safe as *"It seems the only danger is when someone touches it"*. Appeal is approved

item.title: Re: The Midas Brick
item.content:encoded:
Hey again! I see you've responded to my crit!
I'll give you my thoughts on both the options you've presented:

+ Option 1 +
- Close -

This just seems like a random ability tacked onto an (in my opinion) uninteresting concept in an effort to make it appear more interesting. Allow me to reiterate that making an SCP more dangerous does not, I repeat does not make it more interesting. This only serves to break the theme of the object completely. I'd strongly recommend not using this option, as a 'cloud of deadly radiation' has nothing to do with Midas or gold.

+ Option 2 +
- Close -

This option is slightly better than the previous, but still not great. All it does is reanimate people and turn them into hostile, golden killing machines. It's boring and cliche. It also doesn't match with the myth of Midas, which is what you're basing your concept off of. Unless this goes under some heavy reworking, this option won't work either.


Anyway, that's it for this recrit. Hope this helps!

item.title: The Technician's Glasses
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: When worn, you are put in an anti-memetic state and, when viewing any anomaly that seemingly creates matter or energy, you will see a rubber wire leading out of it and into the sky.

Central Narrative: The foundation interacts with the 'electricity' that comes from these wires, until eventually they receive an invoice from the 'Electric Company' advising them to cease experimentation. They are successful in the creation of numerous useful anomalous devices before eventually, a 'Technician' appears in the site and retrieves the glasses before amnesticizing the foundation staff and deleting the file, which is found in data-backlogs by MTF-Rho 9. The item is considered neutralized for the time being.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The file is seemingly still anti-memetic and one needs to be conditioned using memetic images to view it. The underlying narrative of a foundation existing above the foundation responsible for the empowering of Anomalous items is the main hook of the article. Another piece of the puzzle is added to the mystery of where the energy for anomalies come from, with more room for expansion.

item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The scp is a life giving parasite that infect inanimate objects and gives them vital organs and personalities. These instances usually become suicidal and begin to ponder on why they were given life. All instances that the foundation has encountered have been friendly and interactive. as If they were human. The foundation contains them by putting them in separate decompression tanks. They have monitors on the side that keep track of their vital signs. The foundation also keeps track of the lifespan of the infected instances. On one occasion, a parasite left the object. That object: (a toothbrush) was able to continue functioning as a regular tooth brush.

Central Narrative: It is a parasite that gives every day objects the ability to live.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origin of the parasites are unknown. There are currently 110 encounters on the foundation record.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
How about this for a flow of the story:

+ Idea here
- Long, I know
  1. We start off with SCP-XXXX's discovery in 1945 when Farringford House is sold. As well as SCP-XXXX, they also discover a number of old documents which show sketches of SCP-XXXX's mutilations and a log of her time in the home. At the same time, the first recorded incident of SCP-XXXX-1 occurs.
  1. The second incident of SCP-XXXX-1 occurs. Thanks to some decryption of the documents found with SCP-XXXX, the foundation makes the connection between SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1 and containment procedures are created accordingly.
  1. An attempt to get some answers from SCP-XXXX are logged in an interview. She claims she doesn't remember her life before the house and only remembers weaving and her condition came because of a man. She is upset and gives vague answers to the questions before remaining silent. As the interview ends, she asks about the condition of 'Edward'. When they ask who 'Edward' is, SCP-XXXX quiets up again, only saying 'the shadows1 made him sick. Sick on the inside'.
  1. Further documentation about SCP-XXXX is found in Chapel House2. Also found is a logbook which details some of the past SCP-XXXX incidents, the 'decaying' process as well as Edwards descent into mental instability. One entire highlights the success of their endeavours to make SCP-XXXX ageless and give her her eyelid coatings. The logbook also mentions some members of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and their involvement with SCP-XXXX.
  1. The third incident of SCP-XXXX-1 occurs. Following this two, a number of interviews are done with some of the victims. Most are sickened by the event and demonstrate an irrational fear of reflective surfaces. In the interviews, the victims claim their reflections spoke to them, with some screaming with rage, others degrading with vile slander and some just outright maliciously laughing or taunting3.
  1. As a result of SCP-XXXX-1, a number of its victims have developed mental illnesses, depression, severe paranoia or psychosis, even after administering amnestics4. Some have decided into a state of such delirium, they have resorted to making irrational decisions such as removing fingernails, avoiding water or destroying computers and smart devices. A small amount has committed suicide too.
  1. Final interview with SCP-XXXX. After being unresponsive for a few minutes, she begins talking about the shadows. When pressed about why she must remain alive, as her condition seems to cause SCP-XXXX-1, SCP-XXXX provides an answer which enables the foundation to understand that she is in fact preventing SCP-XXXX-1.
  1. Final entry. After a health check-up, researcher's discover that SCP-XXXX's eyelid coating is starting to noticeably decay. Research into recreating the material has begun and adjustments to SCP-XXXX's containment procedure is begin reevaluated. However, the likelihood of SCP-XXXX-1 occurring more frequently is highly possible.
Footnotes
1. The shadows are what The Lady Of Shallot calls the reflections in the poem. "I am half-sick of shadows, said The Lady of Shallot".
2. Another of Tennyson's homes.
3. Think like that crybaby seen in Handmaid's Tale
4. Quoted as saying "They're watching us"

item.title: Re: Living on repeat
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps I should walk through one example really quick. Forgive any typos, I am on mobile atm.

SCP XXXX undergoes some testing with scp 343 and comes through ok. Upon the records being filed with exclusion site, the exclusion site gets a version of this report, let's call it Report 1A. However, later that month a containment breach happens, but SCP XXXX (not uncontained, just in a site during a breach) survives, getting logged in a incident report which we will call 2B.

Upon upload to the exlusion site, they get 3 reports. One copy of report 2B, where scp xxxx survived the breach. The other two reports that appear are Report 1B, where differences might be as minor as different things spoken, and 2A, in which 682 eats scp xxxx during the breach. Upon an interview with researchers present at the first test, they remember events as detailed in report 1B.

This should answer the question of what's going on, as clearly in one reality, he had died in the breach while in the one they currently reside in he lived. Exclusion sites are immune to time shifts, especially at this scale, so they are able to somewhat track his lives through the discrepencies in the report. The only question is if he is creating these realities with every death, or merely exploring them through his choices. The former is a serious threat, while the latter means he is a traveler with the logs acting like pages from a journal left behind.

Containment is as cold as the foundation, using what effectively amounts to brainwashing to ensure that he keeps living life in the same way that led him to the Foundation. Now, they can only really detect this anomaly through the exclusion sites reports (at least at first), so my way to intro him will likely be as a D-class, who just so happens get included in a report that results in a duplicate report being discovered by the exclusion site during routine backups.

As for "what makes this time loop stand out?" There's a few things. Firstly, this is written from an outsider's point of view, being the exlcusion site reports. Secondly, this guy has no exit, unlike most other time loops where eventally they get that escape from infinite repetitions. Thirdly, this guy isn't smart. Bill Murray was mastering all kinds of skills from piano to ice sculpting, but this guys struggles to remember himself. The human brain has limited capacity, and this dude is pretty average at best outside of the anomoly.

The 4th thing as you mentioned is scale. Due to starting as a baby everytime, by the time he becomes a d-class he has made way too many chioces for him to remember perfectly, let alone repeat. This allows the butterfly effect to really have some power compared to day long time loops where you aren't able to change most routines or circumstances.

I hope that answered your questions. This SCP isn't generally going to be as flashy or otherworldly. It's the story of a man living way too long in what amounts to basic human containment in foundation custody. He's not necessarily a direct threat, but his existance poses many problems that the Foundation would prefer to minimize if possible.

item.title: Re: The Phone Book
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open
[-] Close

Lemme hand you some crit:

Central Narrative:

Your narrative here is simply the recovery of the object, not an actual plot.

a serial killer believed to have anomalous abilities.

He kills people well so they think he anomalous properties. His actions are simply not enough to warrant any Foundation attention.

an old phone book which contains the name and current location

Is it alphabetical? Is there a way to search (because if not, how the hell was that serial killer getting anything done)? How are the pages stored, since a book cannot hold millions of pages.

I think what makes this interesting is it kind of explains how the foundation can almost always find people

Or, they are just a very well funded agency. I don't see how the book could even help very much, seeing as you'd need to know someone's name before being able to find them, and how does it show their location, coordinates? Because if so, then the book must've been made after or in the 17th century, and if it was made during the 17th century, how does it conceivably have every person who has ever lived's name in it? And where does the book draw the line between homo sapiens and our closest ancestor? And what if the Foundation is trying to find "John Smith" there would be multiple pages dedicated to different John Smith's.

contains the name

What if somebody legally changes their name, what happens? And how is a persons name decided, does everybody have a special name chosen by God, or does it just write in the name that parents name their babies.

Because the book could be used to discover so many things

… How exactly? It shows the names and locations of people, how could this discover so many things? They could find some corpses, maybe. But considering the way names have worked has changed over the course of thousands of years, I doubt it can be used for anything at all really.

I’m aware I may be a bit vague, but this is really just an idea right now and needs some more fleshing out.

It's very rough, you don't have anything here other than an implausible scenario, a weird book, and allusions to "good things" coming from said book.

Mirroring Sun’s notes above, the dialogue is wooden and we never really get a handle on who these people are or why we should care that they’re affected in this way

Leading from that, this has a lack of real stakes. In all but one recorded instance the individuals eventually move on and don’t recall anything anomalous (so it’s not really even a threat to the Veil)… but why would the foundation expend time and effort in this detailed a report? On a separate note: the crossing out and the black boxes really don’t make sense. As the meta means we’re (as readers) able to can access to the file so why would anything be redacted?

The crossing out is another thing, this is a digital file, so crossing out makes no sense. You can communicate those changes: “it was originally thought that long term containment was impossible but given the events as laid out in ___, this is no longer the case.”

item.title: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Which I actually did by suggesting how it would interact with specific GOI's.

1) As a joke SCP the termites have two things going for them: First, they can access virtually any space. This means that you have a number of potentially fun issues to consider, ranging from interrupting the activities of different groups just by showing up (especially for activities that require the local space not have dimensional anomalies, such as summonings), making sterile spaces not so sterile, and even attacking objects made of wood.

I'm pretty sure an insect that feeds on wood would find wooden anomalies particularly delicious, and could even go a ways towards explaining the termites' ability itself.

Secondly, I went with the pun of offices being literally bugged by the topologically enhanced termites. That is, how the MC&D offices would be bugged by a literal insect rather than a technological device, and that would probably drive MC&D crazy, especially as they consider themselves beyond being affected by SCPs.

It's thus entirely possible that not only would the termites be a problem themselves in the SCP universe, but that you could have animals that preyed on the animal as well as the possibility of pest control officers that either have problems with the termites due to their inability to be killed by normal means or are specifically set up to deal with the termites. Also, there's the possibility of dealing with dead insects where there should be no dead insects due to the ability of some insect poisons to spread from insect to insect.

And keep in mind that there are some diseases spread by insects. In short, the termite's ability to be anywhere and cause chaos is noteworthy. As "it's the fault of termites" could become a catchphrase to explain a wide variety of problems in the SCP universe.

2) Also, various Sarkic cults are into dimensional manipulation; as such an insect that can ignore topological constraints would be well worth looking into, especially if there was any evidence that they went into dimensions not our own would be well worth investigating. It would be interesting to see a specific Sarkic cult based on the worship of these termites.

Conversely, given the Church of the Broken God's belief that no organic life is superior to technology, the termite could be used to poke fun at that belief. At the very least, having a social insect that it can't do anything about would make it the very antithesis of a group dedicated to collective consciousness and technological superiority.

Other GOIs would have similar experiences as MC&D, the Sarkists, and the Church of the Broken God, but these are the most extreme.

3) Not my SCP. As such, I only felt comfortable nudging the author towards checking out the GOIs listed and not actually going full-out in explaining the possibilities. When reviewing in the future, I'll try to keep in mind that I need to REALLY expand on things.

Not much is known about the SCP, except for things like its ability to 'trick' the human mind, but it is thought to be from another place, planet, or possibly even universe, the Foundation cannot specify except the fact that it knows what it is, and possibly where it is from. The effect that it gives needs to be tested on a bit more, as the Foundation doesn't know if it is explainable scientifically as of yet. The ability, or anomalous effect, the SCP has is connected to its nickname and personality, since it has slightly hinted at it, as those who are perfect do not have greed or something they want, this SCP may 'want' something but it does not think like that, it thinks that it can get it because it is perfect. And if the anomalous effect is connected, that means it has no sins or anything imperfect, from its point of view, maybe meaning if you do something that counts as bad or imperfect, also in its point of view, it may be able to get into your head.

item.title: Re: The Click
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a quick look. As a general note, I prefer reading shorter, snappy articles, so given that this draft is over 2700 words, it's not exactly the kind of article I would seek out for entertainment/leisure.

With regards to specifics:

Dialogue. It's not my strong suit and there's a lot of it. Does it work?

I would say not really. I don't get a clear sense of the characters in the first log—SCP-XXXX-1B sometimes reads like a teenager, and SCP-XXXX-1A switches between sounding casual and sounding like a supervisor at the start.

+ show block
– hide block

Does it resonate emotionally?

For me, not really. It feels like the dialogue is just there to be exposition spoonfeeding; the first discussion feels rather wooden; if you want to indicate distance or tension, you can do that without making the characters sound like robots. The people talking don't sound like actual people because their speech seems to be just there to exhibit the effects of the anomaly—there isn't really a consistent characterization at the start, which makes the "changes" in dialogue later on seem like different characters entirely rather than a shift in the conversation.

It also seems unusually plot-convenient that the two people in the Foundation who just happened to "click" also just happen to have dark pasts and PTSD-associated memories.

If not, how to proceed.

Try to get others involved to talk out the dialogue with you. Pay attention to natural inclusions of pauses and "um" or "uh", and ask if what they're saying is something they would say to another person in that situation when they have that role. Also watch for overusage of certain words; you've got a lot of "oh" and "yeah"s in the first log.

Should the very end be removed? I feel like the final monologue could be stupid and/or too revelatory.

I honestly don't really understand what happened at the end. Was the implication that the alleged anomaly is not an actual anomaly, but rather a Foundation cover-up?

If so, how to proceed.

I feel like you'd need to keep it because otherwise readers might just wonder what the point of the anomaly is. When I got to Event Log XXXX-1-BETA, I felt like the entirety of the article I'd already read didn't seem like a Keter-class global-scale anomaly at all since the main recorded incident was at a Foundation site, during a Foundation event that was conveniently under close enough surveillance to distinguish presumably hours of private conversation.

Overall, I personally am not a huge fan of this, mostly because it feels like the core premise is buried under hundreds of words of fluff text. The nearly 670 words of the description feels like a slog at the start of the list of stages—my personal suggestion is that you trim both the conditions and the stages information down a lot. Doing so would better set the stage of the Foundation not knowing a whole lot about the anomaly (which I presume is the case? Otherwise the sheer amount of investigative resources allocated to this thing, with potentially lots of false positives, would be kind of ridiculous, and surely someone would have noticed that there's no reason to amnesticize everyone who happens to suddenly get along well with a stranger? Humans evolved to be gregarious, after all). Also, there would be less of a risk that a reader gets fatigued by the minutiae details and loses interest in finishing the article before they make it past the description.

As another note, there are definitely small errors present, like "relive themselves" instead of "relieve". That's something to address after the other fixes though, presuming you're keen on revising per my personal (not a big fan of long articles) taste. Definitely ask other reviewers what they think, though, if you'd like to keep this near its current wordcount.
